MY AUDIT!

- I feel like the references are not being used fully. Most of the imagery seems to take place on one part of the same ship. I do see some subtle, nuanced elements that may or may not be on this particular cruise ship, but a lot of the defining features of the ship are just not found in the images being generated now. 
- There's probably a lot of conflicting information throughout the system about how many people, if any, to put in these images. The overall overriding rule should be that group action is the priority. While theme details and ship details are important, the theme should be group-driven. The imagery should always have four to six, even ten, people involved in some kind of activity that speaks to the theme of the cruise. This thought process has changed over time based off of the quality of the image generation by the models, but at this point I believe that is less of an issue. 
- There is an overabundance of people sitting at tables, eating and drinking, or staring over a rail. This is fine for 10% of the imagery, but not 90% as I'm saying now. This really points out the need for diversification of the images, specifically diversity in ethnicity and in age. Right now I see the same thirty-something year old white lady and her husband in pretty much every image. 
- We may need to somewhat embellish the activity of the theme cruise, even if it's more than what we might actually see in real life. The way the images are now seems a little bit mundane. Even though they might be, for all intents and purposes, correctly portraying the theme, the images are still coming across as sort of dull and not much activity one way or the other. 
- At first, I was skeptical about embellishment because I didn't want to necessarily false sell anything or over-hype anything, but I'm starting to rethink that logic because the whole idea is to attract the guest's attention, at least when we're dealing with ads. The landing page will sort of calibrate the user's expectations that everything is sort of a potential and not necessarily a given. The landing page will sort of calibrate the user's expectations that everything is sort of a potential and not necessarily a given. 
- We still have some of the "watercolor" images drifting into the hero shots. I am pretty certain we're not going to use any of these, but it may be good to keep them in a specifically unique section where they could be used as alternative images in a specific campaign. But they should not be in the main selected photos that the orchestrator chooses from. 
- I would like to revisit the ideas that we explored earlier of using different sepia tones or black and white or some kind of filters on some of these images, just to give them different looks. 
- From the beginning, freshly generated media/images do no do a good job at portraying 'Theme' of the cruise. For example , for a 'glass-observatory-winter-sea-watchers' campaign slug I do see images of people standing outside looking up at the sky and pointing, but it's obviously off because it's bright daylight outside where it should probably be dusk or pitch black, And what people are looking at is not necessarily prevalent, other than they are just looking at something in the sky. Other examples are of people sitting, holding a cup of coffee, and turning their head to the right to look out the window at the sea, and that's it. The point is, these images are far too bland and indescriptive and too much like your typical type travel enjoyment scenery, which is not what we are aiming for. I expect the system to dig deep into the niche and to pull out very specific and vivid, exciting scenes that directly depict the theme involved, and articulate that in the imagery deeply. 
- The 10 scenes images are, by far, the best and most well-thought-out and articulated images that come closer to what the theme should be. Maybe we should use that as a baseline for all image generations. I like the fact that they look real: I can see people looking up in the sky, and the sky is somewhat dark. I see a big group of people in the distance around the pool, which is very realistic looking, unlike the other one or two people on a huge ship images that I'm getting in the heroes and concepts.
- What I don't have much use for is the theater image in the scenes, as it never looks realistic. It always looks forced, and we probably don't need a theater scene in every campaign. Just maybe in campaigns that would actually involve theater activity. 
- The destination port scene is dumb because it's always showing people on a deck overlooking a rail, which is what 70% of all other images do anyway. There's too much rail overlooking. Since I'm actually thinking about it, the destination port image is dumb. We don't need to see the destination port because it's really just a takeoff port, and there's nothing to see. Let's remove that. Nightclub scene similar to theater. Don't always need it. Don't really need it. It looks forced most of the time. 
- For the documentary details We need to be more creative with the image style, like:
- grain photo
- sepia tones
- contrast curves
- overlays
- color alterations
- hue adjustments
things like that.

- All of the images are bright daylight. We need a good mix of different times of day, as well as different ethnicities and ages of people. This is important. 
- All imagery and photography should have an artistic flair to it overall. Not so mundane, not so bland, not so photorealistic in the normal sense. We don't want it to look unbelievable, but we do want to embellish.
